doc: Log-log slope of the radially averaged power spectrum: (patch - mean) * Hann (np.hanning(n) outer itself, symmetric, 0.5 - 0.5 cos(2 pi i / (n - 1))), np.fft.fft2 (unnormalized, complex128), fftshift, |F|^2, radius r = int(hypot(x, y)) with x, y counted from n // 2 (truncation), radial[r] = mean of the power at integer radius r (np.bincount), wavelength of bin k = n * patch_px_km() / k km; bins with lo <= wavelength <= hi (inclusive) and radial > 0 enter np.polyfit(log k, log radial, 1), whose slope is returned; fewer than 4 bins give NaN. n = patch.shape[0] (square patches only). A synthetic field with a k^-3 spectrum (random phases, n = 64): the fitted slope is near -3 (the Hann window and the radial truncation bias it). The whole chain is float64 (the Hann window is float64 even for a float32 patch): an independent float64 reimplementation agrees to 9e-16 with np.fft and to 1.4e-13 with an explicit DFT-matrix product (a different operation order; measured on Earth patches, noise and smooth fields), a float64 one-ulp nudge of the texels moves the slope by <= 1.7e-15; tolerance 1e-9.
